templateDescBasicQa: Select two blocks to create a card. The first block is the question, the second is the answer.
templateDescBidirectional: Select two blocks to create two cards that are each other's question and answer.
templateDescListItem:
Generates cards from both ordered and unordered list children. Right-click a list item block to use. Ordered children are generated progressively; unordered children are summarized. Supports per-child hints separated by 【→】.
Example:
  • (Any parent block)
    1. Question→Answer
    2. Term→Definition
templateDescListConceptMultiline:
CDF `:::` multiline card mode. Ordered and unordered child items are processed the same way. The parent block must include a referenced concept document. [Select the list-item block that contains the concept reference.]
Example:
  • [[Neutron Star]]:::
    • Remains left after a stellar explosion
    • Formed through a nova event
templateDescListDescriptorMultiline:
CDF `;;;` multiline card mode. Ordered and unordered child items are processed the same way. The concept is auto-found by upward search. [Select the list-item block where the descriptor is located.]
Example:
  • [[Neutron Star]]
    • Formation process;;;
      1. Precursor→star
      2. Phase→late stage
templateDescConceptDescriptor:
Batch-create concept definition and attribute cards. Place block references in a list using transclusion links.
Example: Mixed definitions and descriptors
  • [[Neutron Star]]::An extremely dense object between a white dwarf and a black hole
    • Origin;; Remnant core of 8–30 solar mass stars
    • Density ;; A teaspoon weighs ~1 billion tons
Symbols:
• Definition (top-level ref): 【::】bidirectional, 【:>】forward, 【:<】reverse
• Descriptor (children): 【;;】forward, 【;<】reverse, 【;<>】bidirectional
templateDescDescriptorAuto:
Select a block containing descriptor symbols to create a descriptor card. Automatically finds the parent concept block.
Supports: 【;;】forward, 【;<】reverse, 【;<>】bidirectional
templateDescMultiCloze:
Each marker generates one independent card.
Example: Gather==all== wisdom, benefit==all== people
templateDescConceptDefinition:
Creates bidirectional cards for a concept and its definition. Use a block reference with 【::】 to separate the definition.
Example: [[Neutron Star]]::An extremely dense object between a white dwarf and a black hole
templateDescConceptDefinitionForward:
Creates a forward card for concept and definition using 【:>】.
Example: [[Neutron Star]]:>An extremely dense object
templateDescConceptDefinitionReverse:
Creates a reverse card for concept and definition using 【:<】.
Example: [[Neutron Star]]:
templateDescConceptDescriptorReverse:
Creates a reverse card for concept and descriptor using 【;<】.
Example: attribute;
templateDescConceptDescriptorBoth:
Creates bidirectional cards for concept and descriptor using 【;<>】.
Example: attribute;<>description
templateDescQuickCard:
Generate a single card from one block using symbols.
Example: Question>>Answer
templateDescBidirectionalSingle:
Generate two reciprocal cards from one block using the <> symbol.
Example: TermA<>TermB

aiTutorPromptPresetAudience: For the present self roaming through neural review.
aiTutorPromptPresetBehavior: It behaves more like a study companion that keeps the thinking moving instead of locking the material too early.
aiTutorPromptPresetOutput: Provides an editable behavior prompt and follow-up prompt pair; structured output rules are appended by the system.
aiExplainPromptPresetAudience: For the present self reviewing a card, acting like a compressed understanding coach rather than an encyclopedia article.
aiExplainPromptPresetBehavior: It emphasizes working definitions, causality, boundaries, connections, and triggers; it can mention the answer conditionally but does not lazily restate it.
aiExplainPromptPresetOutput: Provides an editable behavior prompt and follow-up prompt pair; structured output rules are appended by the system.
aiConceptCoachPromptPresetTitle: Recommended AI Understand & Make Cards Template
aiConceptCoachPromptPresetAudience: For a self who already knows a little and now wants to truly understand the concept, with the goal of recalling, distinguishing, and applying it later.
aiConceptCoachPromptPresetBehavior: Start with a working definition, build understanding through five angles, then generate self-test candidates and real-world triggers without padding weak cards.
aiConceptCoachPromptPresetOutput: Each stage still has editable prompts; runtime output stays structured JSON, and self-test cards use canonical fields instead of mode-specific markdown.
aiCardPromptPresetAudience: For your future reviewing self, aiming to extract a small number of high-value candidate cards from the current material.
aiCardPromptPresetBehavior: It prioritizes distinctions, causality, applications, boundaries, and triggers while keeping quality above count.
aiCardPromptPresetOutput: Provides an editable behavior prompt and follow-up prompt pair; structured output rules are appended by the system.
aiCdfPromptPresetAudience: For your future reviewing self, using CDF to anchor concepts first and then split reusable descriptor dimensions.
aiCdfPromptPresetBehavior: It prioritizes concept definitions, traits, mechanisms, conditions, evidence, contrasts, and examples instead of mechanically shredding the source.
aiCdfPromptPresetOutput: Provides an editable behavior prompt and follow-up prompt pair; structured output rules are appended by the system.

aiTutorDescription: More like a study companion that thinks with you than a tool that summarizes too early.
aiTutorHeadline: Read the current neural roam path and surface patterns, tensions, and next directions
aiTutorHelper: Prioritizes the current node, current path position, current card, and recent path history.
aiTutorEmptyBody: Useful when you want to pause during neural roaming and let AI point out blind spots and promising threads.
aiTutorBullet1: It does not default to writing a formal summary for you.
aiTutorBullet2: The goal is to help you keep building an implicit knowledge network.
aiTutorBullet3: After reading it, you can still decide whether anything deserves candidate cards.
aiTutorDockHint: It gives you a sense of direction first, then you decide whether to formalize anything.
aiTutorFollowUpHint: Ask about a thread, a tension, or why this batch is worth roaming further.
aiExplainDescription: Explain the current card by placing it back into its original knowledge network.
aiExplainHeadline: Explain what it tests, why it is hard, and which knowledge cluster it belongs to
aiExplainHelper: In review mode it respects the reveal boundary so AI does not become a spoiler.
aiExplainEmptyBody: Useful after reveal when you want to understand why this card matters and what material it connects to.
aiExplainBullet1: The goal is not to restate the answer, but to explain why the card is framed this way.
aiExplainBullet2: It tries to stay grounded in the current card and its source blocks.
aiExplainBullet3: If the explanation surfaces good ideas, you can turn them into candidate cards directly.
aiExplainDockHint: Reveal first, then explain, to stay aligned with retrieval practice.
aiExplainFollowUpHint: Ask about its boundaries, causality, what old ideas it gets confused with, or what situations should trigger recall next time.
aiMakeCardsDescription: Generate candidate cards from the current material, then prune, edit, save them into Daily Note, and only create them at the end.
aiMakeCardsDescriptionConfiguredStorage: Generate candidate cards from the current material, then prune, edit, save them into the configured storage, and only create them at the end.
aiMakeCardsHeadline: Keep AI in the role of drafting candidates and saving drafts instead of writing cards directly into your system
aiMakeCardsHelper: Write confirmed candidates into today's Daily Note first, then create cards from those concrete draft blocks.
aiMakeCardsHelperConfiguredStorage: Write confirmed candidates into the configured draft area first, then create cards from those concrete draft blocks.
aiMakeCardsEmptyBody: Useful when you select a group of blocks in the browser or continue from explanation into candidate generation, then explicitly save drafts before creating cards.
aiMakeCardsBullet1: Choose a mode and generate candidates first.
aiMakeCardsBullet2: Each candidate can be lightly edited, discarded, kept, and then saved into Daily Note.
aiMakeCardsBullet2ConfiguredStorage: Each candidate can be lightly edited, discarded, kept, and then saved into the configured storage.
aiMakeCardsBullet3: Only saved drafts go through the existing card creation path.
aiMakeCardsDockTitle: Three steps: generate, save draft, create
aiMakeCardsDockHint: Daily Note draft blocks become the direct card-face source so AI candidates and final cards stay aligned.
aiMakeCardsDockHintConfiguredStorage: Draft blocks in the configured storage become the direct card-face source so AI candidates and final cards stay aligned.
aiMakeCardsFollowUpHint: Ask why a candidate was split this way, whether another template fits better, or to shrink it into fewer, steadier cards.
aiMakeCardsCdfDescription: Use CDF to anchor concepts first, then split high-value descriptor dimensions into steadier concept-definition / descriptor candidates.
aiMakeCardsCdfHeadline: Let AI find the concept first, then turn the material into candidate cards through descriptor dimensions
aiMakeCardsCdfHelper: Prioritizes concept definitions, boundaries, traits, mechanisms, conditions, evidence, contrasts, and examples while staying on the existing draft-save and card-creation path.
aiMakeCardsCdfEmptyBody: Useful when you face a dense passage and want CDF to extract concept anchors plus stable descriptors before deciding what truly deserves a card.
aiMakeCardsCdfBullet1: Start by finding concept anchors and stable working definitions.
aiMakeCardsCdfBullet2: Then extract high-value descriptor dimensions such as boundaries, mechanisms, conditions, evidence, contrasts, and examples.
aiMakeCardsCdfBullet3: Finally remove filler so only candidates that support stable recall remain.
aiMakeCardsCdfDockTitle: Three steps: concept anchors, descriptor dimensions, candidate cards
aiMakeCardsCdfDockHint: CDF results still save to drafts first, then flow through the existing concept-definition / descriptor creation path.
aiMakeCardsCdfFollowUpHint: Ask whether the concept anchor is stable, which descriptor dimensions should be removed, or whether a concept-definition or concept-descriptor template fits better.
